plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether fine-scale thickness tuning around a proven 22-layer ZnS/Al2O3 topology can extract additional spectral performance in dual-band mid-IR transmission filtering. The prior knowledge basis is that quarter-wave-inspired stacks with high/low index alternation create stopbands, while strategic thickness deviations create transmission windows. This route refines the best candidate from iteration 16 by constraining thickness perturbations to ±15 nm, transitioning from global exploration to local interference optimization. No literature was consulted; this draws on recalled thin-film physics about constructive/destructive interference tuning.

routes.title: Local thickness refinement of 22-layer ZnS/Al2O3 dual-band mid-IR filter on Daimon-20 substrate
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Constraining thickness perturbations to ±15 nm around the iteration-16 best candidate will improve target score by resolving fine-scale interference conditions without disrupting the established macroscopic topology that already achieves ~0.92 target performance.
routes.design_principle: Recalled thin-film physics: transmission peaks in multilayer stacks arise from constructive interference at specific wavelengths, controlled by optical path lengths (n×d). Small thickness adjustments (~λ/100 scale at mid-IR) can shift phase relationships enough to improve passband transmission while maintaining stopband rejection. The 22-layer ZnS/Al2O3 alternation provides sufficient degrees of freedom for dual-band optimization.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | ZnS | Al2O3 | Daimon-20 substrate (22 coating layers total)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses, each constrained to ±15 nm around the iteration-16 best candidate values
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm band (methane)
Maximize mean transmittance in 4200-4300 nm band (carbon dioxide)
Minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm band (suppression)
Minimize mean transmittance in 4450-5000 nm band (suppression)
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 22 (within 24-layer limit)
ZnS and Al2O3 are conventional depositable IR materials
Thickness tolerances of ±15 nm are achievable with modern deposition monitoring
theory_basis: Recalled: High/low index alternation creates photonic stopbands via Bragg reflection
Recalled: Transmission windows can be engineered by breaking periodicity with strategic thickness variations
Recalled: Mid-IR wavelengths (3-5 μm) require layer thicknesses on order of 500-1500 nm for quarter-wave conditions
Recalled: ZnS has higher refractive index (~2.2-2.4 in mid-IR) than Al2O3 (~1.6-1.7), providing sufficient index contrast
Recalled: CaF2 (Daimon-20 dataset) is transparent in mid-IR and serves as suitable substrate
expected_advantages: Focused local search avoids wasting iterations on topologically inferior regions
±15 nm constraint preserves the macroscopic interference pattern already optimized
Fine tuning may resolve phase mismatches that limit the 0.9202 score
Maintains material pair consistency for fair comparison across control route iterations
known_risks: Uncertain whether ±15 nm window is wide enough to escape local optima - if no improvement occurs, widening to ±30 nm would need to be tested
Recalled ZnS and Al2O3 mid-IR extinction coefficients are approximate; actual absorption may limit achievable transmittance
Uncertain whether 22 layers is optimal vs. fewer layers with different topology - but changing layer count would be a different axis
Daimon-20 substrate refractive index dispersion in mid-IR not precisely recalled; registry data will resolve this
No polarization or angle specification in original request; assuming normal incidence which may not match actual sensor geometry
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer planar multilayer filter on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat), ZnS, Al2O3 (Kischkat) (22 coating layers). Initialize thicknesses at: [909.4, 804.2, 708.0, 683.0, 344.8, 1221.0, 362.2, 576.3, 876.3, 627.6, 371.9, 1154.2, 336.7, 467.5, 850.9, 419.4, 829.2, 1274.1, 929.2, 420.9, 806.8, 881.9] nm (iteration-16 best candidate). Constrain each thickness to ±15 nm around these center values. Optimize for: maximize mean transmittance in 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm bands; minimize mean transmittance in 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm bands. Use coherent transfer matrix method. Normal incidence, unpolarized. No metal layers. Total layer count fixed at 22.
routes.revision_reason: Transition from global exploration to focused local search: constrain perturbation amplitudes to ±15 nm centered on the iteration-16 best candidate to resolve fine-scale constructive interference conditions without disrupting the established macroscopic topology.

plan.knowledge_source_disclosure: This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone. No Semantic Scholar query was issued, no retrieved paper reached the prompt, and no method-research report was supplied -- neither for the initial plan nor for any continuation round. It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against the literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.
unresolved_decisions: Whether ±15 nm is the optimal perturbation scale for mid-IR thickness tuning - this would require empirical testing across multiple scales
Exact mid-IR refractive index dispersion curves for ZnS and Al2O3 - registry data will provide measured values
Whether normal incidence assumption matches actual sensor optical geometry - would need payload specification
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route cannot exceed 0.92 target score after 3 refinement rounds with relaxed constraints, the limitation is likely topological (material pair or layer count) rather than thickness optimization, and a different axis would be needed.

expected_observations: If hypothesis holds: best_target_score should increase from 0.9202 toward 0.93+ over 2-3 rounds while tightest_margin remains stable or improves
If hypothesis fails: best_target_score should plateau within 1e-3 of 0.9202 despite constrained optimization, indicating the topology itself limits further improvement
valid_candidates should remain high (≥5) since ±15 nm constraints keep designs near physically valid region
thicknesses_nm should show small deviations from center values, not wholesale restructuring
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If tightest_margin falls below 0.30 consistently across rounds, relax the ±15 nm constraint to ±30 nm and continue
If valid_candidates drops below 3 for two consecutive rounds, widen thickness bounds to ±25 nm and recenter on the best valid candidate

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
